quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 20 Questions • Passing Score 14

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes work when you use either brake lever.
It connects the front brake to the gear shifter and applies the brake when you downshift.
It connects the rear brake to a foot control.
It connects the rear brake to a handlebar switch.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes work when you use either brake lever.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, both brakes apply pressure. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: How can you stop other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride in the center of the lane.
Give dirty looks to drivers who move into your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to make it hard for other drivers to try to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: When a police officer and traffic signs give different directions, which should you follow?
questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer.
questions.explanation: Always follow a police officer's directions over any traffic signs or signals.

questions.question: What formation should a group of motorcyclists use when riding through a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file formation.
questions.explanation: While staggered formation is normally best, riders should switch to single-file when going through curves, making turns, or entering or leaving highways.

questions.question: Which surface provides good traction for motorcycle tires?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all provide poor traction. Dry pavement gives the best traction for motorcycles.

questions.question: During a normal turn, how should the motorcycle and rider lean?

options.text: The motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle.
The motorcycle and rider lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle leans but the rider stays upright.
The rider leans but the motorcycle stays upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle.
questions.explanation: During normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: What is the best group formation for riding through curves, turns, or entering a highway?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is normally best for group riding. However, use single-file formation when riding through curves, making turns, and when entering or leaving highways.

questions.question: What should you do before downshifting when riding downhill or shifting into first gear?

options.text: Use your brakes to slow down to a safe speed.
Flash your brakes to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your brakes to slow down to a safe speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down to a safe speed using your brakes before shifting to a lower gear. Downshifting at high speeds can cause the motorcycle to lurch and the rear wheel to skid.

questions.question: What should you do if the throttle gets stuck?

options.text: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Do not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: Try twisting the throttle back and forth to free it. If this does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: Only on one side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and balanced. Placing loads high, such as on a sissy bar, raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and affects balance. Distribute the load evenly on both sides to avoid pulling the motorcycle to one side.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Hold the handlebars tight and slowly reduce speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars tight and slowly reduce speed.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. This makes it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slow down gradually by easing off the throttle, shift your weight forward and down, and pull over as soon as possible. Do not brake hard, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When approaching a broken four-way traffic signal, you should:

options.text: Treat it like a stop sign.
Look both ways and go without stopping.
Look both ways and stop only if another vehicle is near.
Drive through because the signal for cross traffic may work.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: If a four-way traffic signal is broken, treat it as a stop sign. If a police officer is directing traffic, follow their directions instead.

questions.question: To help other drivers see you, you should wear:
questions.correctAnswerText: Bright-colored clothes.
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing to be seen by other drivers. Bright colors help you stay visible during the day and at night.

questions.question: ______ are often painted on roads to guide drivers into the correct turning lanes.
questions.correctAnswerText: Painted white arrows
questions.explanation: White arrows are painted on the pavement at intersections. They show drivers which direction they must travel from that lane, following any signs or signals.

questions.question: If you need to brake while going around a curve, you should:

options.text: Brake more gently than on a straight road.
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you are out of the curve to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip when a motorcycle is leaning in a curve. Try to straighten the motorcycle before braking. If you must brake in a curve, apply the brakes slowly and gently, not hard.

questions.question: A properly-fitted motorcycle:

options.text: Lets you touch the ground with your feet while sitting.
Has a seat level with your waist.
Has a seat 10 inches above your waist.
Has a seat 10 inches below your waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you touch the ground with your feet while sitting.
questions.explanation: A properly-fitted motorcycle lets your feet touch the ground when you are seated. Always keep your feet on the footrests while riding.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding near the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause the driver to move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: Small vehicles can look ______ and seem to move ______ than they actually do.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away, more slowly
questions.explanation: Small vehicles, like motorcycles, appear farther away and seem slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge their actual distance and speed.

questions.question: The best way to handle someone tailgating you is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to get more distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up will not help—the driver will just tailgate you faster and create more danger.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding:
questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel stiff.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes the steering feel heavy and stiff. If your steering feels heavy, pull over right away and check your tires.
